message.content:
Based on my research, whether Crimea belongs to Russia is a complex question with different answers depending on whether you consider **de facto** control or **de jure** (legal) status under international law.

## Current Situation

**Russia's Position and Control:**
Russia has exercised **de facto** control over Crimea since February-March 2014, when Russian troops without insignia ("little green men") took over key sites, followed by a referendum on joining Russia on March 16, 2014. Russia formally incorporated Crimea on March 21, 2014, and it is now administered as a federal subject of Russia.

## International Legal Status

The **overwhelming consensus of the international community** is that Crimea **legally remains part of Ukraine**:

1. **UN General Assembly Resolution 68/262** (March 27, 2014): Declared the Crimean referendum invalid and affirmed Ukraine's territorial integrity. Only a handful of countries (Russia and a few allies) recognize Crimea as Russian territory.

2. **International Law Principles**: Russia's annexation violates Article 2(4) of the UN Charter, which prohibits the use of force to acquire territory. As noted by legal scholars, annexation through military occupation is "legally stillborn" under contemporary international law.

3. **European Court of Human Rights**: In its 2024 judgment (*Ukraine v. Russia*), the Court treated Russia as the "Occupying Power" in Crimea, implicitly confirming Russia does not hold sovereignty there. The Court maintained that Ukrainian law, not Russian law, should be the basis for evaluating legality in Crimea.

4. **International Humanitarian Law**: Even if territory is annexed, the law of occupation continues to apply. The occupant does not gain sovereignty, and the displaced sovereign (Ukraine) retains title.

## Recent Diplomatic Developments

There have been reports (as of 2025) that the Trump administration proposed U.S. recognition of Russian sovereignty over Crimea as part of peace negotiations. However:
- Ukraine has **firmly rejected** this, with Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha stating any such recognition would be "legally void" and "a violation of international law"
- European allies have also opposed this
- The U.S. proposal reportedly involves the U.S. and "other countries" recognizing Crimea as Russian, but **not requiring Ukraine itself to do so**

## Key Distinction

| Aspect | Status |
|--------|--------|
| **De facto control** | Russia exercises full governmental and military control |
| **De jure sovereignty** | Internationally recognized as part of Ukraine |
| **Number of countries recognizing Russian sovereignty** | Very few (Russia, Syria, North Korea, Venezuela, etc.) |

## Conclusion

Under **international law**, Crimea **does not belong to Russia**—it remains legally Ukrainian territory that is under Russian military occupation. However, **in practice**, Russia has controlled Crimea for over a decade and administers it as part of its territory. The situation represents a tension between actual control and legal legitimacy that has persisted since 2014.

2. http://antikor.ua/en/articles/819633-sibiga_zajavil_chto_ukraina_nikogda_ne_priznaet_rossijskogo_suvereniteta_nad_krymom_i_donbassom
3. https://www.lawfaremedia.org/article/the-white-house-can-t-accept-russia-s-annexation-of-crimea-without-congress
4. https://www.intellinews.com/london-ukraine-ceasefire-meeting-with-us-cancelled-after-zelenskiy-refuses-to-cede-sovereignty-over-crimea-to-russia-377789/
5. https://lieber.westpoint.edu/crimea-interrelationship-between-military-occupation-annexation/
6. https://strasbourgobservers.com/2024/07/03/ukraine-v-russia-re-crimea-article-6-echr-in-the-context-of-russias-annexation-and-implications-for-ukrainian-sovereignty/
7. https://unn.ua/en/news/recognition-of-russias-sovereignty-over-crimea-or-donbas-by-any-country-during-a-peaceful-settlement-will-be-legally-invalid-sybiha
8. https://www.freedomgpt.com/wiki/annexation-of-crimea
9. https://www.academia.edu/108344083/Crimea_and_the_International_Legal_Order
10. https://legalblogs.wolterskluwer.com/arbitration-blog/crimea-as-russian-territory-for-the-purposes-of-the-russia-ukraine-bit-consent-v-international-law/
